why: A directive draws a boundary: bots must not control player tanks in the campaign unless campaign bot players are enabled by a dev flag. The rule is enforced TWICE on purpose -- hud.ts decides whether to OFFER the 'bot' candidate, loop.ts decides whether to PERFORM the reassignment -- so neither half's mutation proves the other, and this entry covers the loop half specifically. That is the half that matters if a caller ever reaches reassignSlot without going through the panel (a stale DOM node, or new wiring): a rule enforced only by the code that draws the buttons is one caller away from not being a rule. Caught by 2 of the 270 cases in loop.test.ts -- the refusal test (a fresh setControllers push appears where none should) and the previous-source test, which distinguishes 'refused' from 'bounced to none': `reassign` sends a displaced slot to 'none', so a guard placed AFTER the reassign call would still corrupt the slot instead of leaving it alone.
killedBy: startGameWith: bots may not drive a player tank in the campaign (boundary enforcement) leaves the refused slot on its previous source, not on none
